The denominator is $3+2\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $3-2\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $3-2\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-6}{3+2\text{i}} & =\frac{-6}{3+2\text{i}}\cdot \frac{3-2\text{i}}{3-2\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-18+12\text{i}}{{3}^{2}-(2\text{i})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-18+12\text{i}}{9-(-4)} \\  & =\frac{-18+12\text{i}}{13}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-18+12\text{i}}{13}=(-\frac{18}{13})+(\frac{12}{13})\,\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
